title: Design a caregiving coordinator
description: A system that turns your caregiving notes into a shared status log, task list, and family update, with urgent items flagged first.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

slack.title: Slack
slack.content: The team messaging app most companies run on. In Level 2, students connect Slack to their AI tools to trigger workflows from messages, post AI-generated updates to channels, or summarize threads automatically.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

children.text: 63 million Americans provide unpaid family care for a relative, averaging 27 hours a week, per [AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving's Caregiving in the US 2025 report](https://www.aarp.org/pri/topics/ltss/family-caregiving/caregiving-in-the-us-2025/). Most families run that second job with no shared system, so siblings each see a different slice of what's happening.

This system turns today's caregiving notes into an updated status log, task assignments split across whoever's involved, and a drafted family update, triggered by a new appointment, a medication change, or a missed-dose alert. It's the highest-stakes build in this catalog. A missed dose has real consequences, so urgent items get flagged first, in plain language, before anything else.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) after every update, a saved [skill](#tooltip-skill) kept in your notes app, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that watches wherever notes already land and posts the family update to your group chat.

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming what needs tracking, who's involved and their responsibilities, how urgent issues get flagged, and where information lives today.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that helps me coordinate care for a family member. Ask me questions, one at a time, about what needs tracking, who's involved and their responsibilities, how urgent issues get flagged, and where information lives today. When you have what you need, write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview surfaces who's responsible for what before a gap causes a missed task, and the scope document becomes the brief every family member can build from.

items: Where the shared log lives so every sibling can read and edit it.
How urgent alerts reach people who don't check the log daily.
Who has final say on what the system surfaces, since it organizes what you tell it and never diagnoses anything on its own.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first in a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model). Common connectors are shared docs or a task board (Google Docs, [Notion](#tooltip-notion), Trello), a calendar (Google Calendar), and messaging for siblings and the care team (iMessage, WhatsApp, [Slack](#tooltip-slack)). The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build your system and test it on today's caregiving notes. The prompt below is an example. Your scope document gives a version for your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Turn today's caregiving notes into an updated status log and task list split across the people involved.

Context: [Paste today's notes.] People involved: [names and roles].

Rules:
- Flag urgent items (missed dose, fall, new symptom) first, in plain language, with no medical interpretation.
- Assign each task to whoever covers that area; mark "unassigned" if it's unclear.
- Append to the log. Never overwrite prior entries.
- Draft a short, factual family update.
- Output as: Urgent Flags, Task Assignments table (Task | Owner | Due), Family Update Draft.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: append-only logging keeps a full record as different siblings update it, and separating urgent flags from routine tasks means nobody has to read the whole log to catch what matters today.

children.text: **Review.** Check the output against your scope. Urgent items flagged first, every task assigned or marked unassigned, log appended rather than overwritten?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what went wrong and fold each correction into the rules.

items: Cross-check medications against pharmacy refill dates.
Build a weekly rollup for a sibling who lives farther away.
Feed the symptom log into a brief for the next doctor's visit.
Connect the shared log and calendar through a [tool connector](#tooltip-tool-connectors) so updates sync without manual copying.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat turn the scope document into pass/fail checks and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each status update, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, urgent flags raised, flags that turned out to matter, tasks assigned, and what rule I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the guesswork over what counts as urgent, and the log columns show which tasks keep landing on the same person before that becomes a pattern nobody named.

children.text: **Log** every run against the rubric. Each entry takes a minute. Note the date, which rubric checks passed or failed, and what you changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from the log. Once the rubric passes a couple weeks straight, package the prompt and rules into a skill. A check that keeps failing is a candidate for its own skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s skill-creator skill writes it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).

One durable failure mode. It only works if the input method is nearly frictionless, since a coordinator nobody updates goes stale within days. Treat every output as organizing notes. It never replaces medical judgment.
